turns.learner: Hello! I want to practise understanding unknown words when I read a story in English.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good choice. Reading stories, we often meet words we do not know.

Here is an example: "The crowd was huge; thousands of people filled the street." Huge means very big. The words "thousands of people" help us guess it.

Words around an unknown word are called clues. When you meet a new word in a story, what do you usually do? Tell me in your own words.

turns.learner: I usually look the word in my dictionary and take the first meaning. Then I continue reading the story.
turns.tutor:
Thank you. A dictionary is a useful tool. Taking the first meaning is true sometimes, but many English words have more than one meaning, so the first one may not fit your story.

Look again at the example: "The crowd was huge; thousands of people filled the street."

Which words in that sentence helped you understand "huge"? Please write them.

turns.learner: The words are thousands of people and filled the street. So huge means very big, I think.
turns.tutor:
Good work. You found clues in the sentence: "thousands of people" and "filled the street". Your guess, "very big", also fits.

One question about your thinking: how do those words make you think of "very big"? Please explain in one or two short sentences.

turns.learner: Because thousands of people is a lot of people, so the crowd must be very big. It fills the street.
turns.tutor:
Yes, that is clear thinking. You used the words around "huge" to work out its meaning, and you explained your reason well.

Now try an exercise.

What does "miserable" mean here? A) very happy B) very sad C) very fast. Reply with the letter only.

Yes, B is correct. Well done.

Now here is a new one to try by yourself.

What does "fair" mean here? A) a funfair B) light in colour C) treating everyone the same. Reply with the letter only.

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: A. Fair is a place with games, I know this word very well.
turns.tutor:
Thank you for explaining. You are right that the place with games is one meaning of "fair". But a word can have several meanings, and the sentence around it decides which one fits, not the meaning you know best.

Please tell me in your own words: what were you thinking when you chose A?
